{{Short description|Peak or top of a geometric figure}}
In [[geometry]], an '''apex''' ({{plural form}}: '''apices''') is the [[Vertex (geometry)|vertex]] which is in some sense the "highest" of the figure to which it belongs. The term is typically used to refer to the vertex opposite from some "[[Base (geometry)|base]]". The word is derived from the [[Latin]] for 'summit, peak, tip, top, extreme end'. The term apex may be used in different contexts:
* In an [[isosceles triangle]], the apex is the vertex where the two sides of equal length meet, opposite the unequal third side.{{r|ghm}}
[[File:Isosceles_triangle_el.svg|thumb|Here the point A is the apex]]
* In a [[Pyramid (geometry)|pyramid]] or [[Cone (geometry)|cone]], the apex is the vertex at the "top" (opposite the [[Base (geometry)|base]]). In a pyramid, the vertex is the point that is part of all the lateral faces, or where all the lateral edges meet.{{r|jacobs}}
[[Image:pyramid.svg|thumb|The apex and base of a square pyramid]]
